definition: A buried provision in corponation employment or residency contracts that nullifies all worker protections, injury compensation, and identity continuity rights in the event of 'operational exigency' — essentially a legal license to dispose of employees without consequence. Axiom Industries and Arcturus Defense Solutions are notorious for their void clauses.
origin: Corporate legal terminology, leaked into public consciousness through Diaspora whistleblower drops
usage: Labor lawyers, street activists, wage slaves reading the fine print, fixers negotiating extractions
example: He signed the Arcturus contract without reading it — three years later they invoked the void clause and he had no name, no record, no recourse.
